items.title: The Five Pillars of Islam have a strict canonical order
items.claim: What is the standard order of the Five Pillars of Sunni Islam?

options.text: Shahada (declaration of faith), Salah (five daily prayers), Zakat (almsgiving), Sawm (fasting in Ramadan), Hajj (pilgrimage to Mecca, once if able)
There is no fixed order; lists vary by region

items.reveal:
The Hadith of Gabriel (recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) lists them in this order. The Shahada is the doorway — 'There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the messenger of God'.

Shia Islam (Twelver tradition) frames the obligations differently — they recognise the practices but list them as part of the Ten Ancillaries (Furu al-Din), alongside jihad, enjoining good and forbidding wrong.

Zakat is typically 2.5% of accumulated wealth annually; Sawm requires no food, drink or marital relations from dawn to sunset in Ramadan.
items.why: Religious practice is not a generic 'doing good'. Islam has specific, ordered obligations with detailed theological rationale — exam answers that treat the Pillars as interchangeable miss the structure.

items.title: Muslims believe the Quran was revealed via the angel Gabriel
items.claim: How do Muslims understand the Quran's origin?

options.text: Muhammad's wise sayings, gathered over centuries
The direct word of God, revealed to Muhammad through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) over 23 years (610-632 CE), to be recited and transmitted unchanged in Arabic
A revised version of the Bible adapted for Arabia

items.reveal:
The word 'Quran' comes from the Arabic root q-r-' meaning 'to recite'. The first revelation (Sura 96, 'Iqra' — 'Recite!') is dated to around 610 CE at the Cave of Hira on Mount Jabal al-Nour.

The Quran was compiled in written form under the third caliph Uthman (around 650 CE), with non-conforming versions destroyed to ensure a single authoritative text. Muslims regard only the Arabic text as the Quran proper; translations are 'meanings of' the Quran.

The Hadith — sayings of Muhammad — is a separate category, compiled by his companions and successors. Major Sunni collections: Sahih al-Bukhari (d. 870) and Sahih Muslim (d. 875).
items.why: The Quran's status differs from how Christians understand the Bible. Islamic theology treats every Arabic word as direct divine speech — which is why translation is always 'the meaning of' rather than 'the Quran'.

items.title: William James identified four marks of mystical experience
items.claim: What are James's four marks of mystical experience?

options.text: Ineffability (cannot be fully described), noetic quality (provides knowledge), transiency (does not last long), passivity (the subject feels acted upon) — set out in 'The Varieties of Religious Experience' (1902)

items.reveal:
James's Gifford Lectures (1901-02) became 'The Varieties of Religious Experience'. He aimed to study religion empirically as a phenomenon of consciousness, regardless of any metaphysical truth claims.

His four marks were intended as descriptive criteria, not arguments for divine reality. Richard Swinburne ('The Existence of God', 1979) and others later used religious experience evidentially — the principle of credulity (we should believe perceptions unless we have reason not to) and the principle of testimony.

Critics including Walter Kaufmann and Steven Katz have argued that mystical experience is heavily shaped by prior cultural framework — a Buddhist's experience is structured by Buddhist concepts.
items.why: Religious experience is studied both descriptively (what do people report?) and evaluatively (what does it prove?). James's framework remains the starting point for both — a century of subsequent debate has built on his typology.
